page.title: Virtual event platform comparison guide
page.description: Compare virtual event platforms by format, cost model, ownership and production needs to choose the right tool for webinars, summits and hybrid conferences.
page.h1: How do you compare virtual event platform options
page.definition: A virtual event platform is software that hosts live, recorded or hybrid experiences for audiences ranging from small webinars to large conferences, providing streaming, registration, engagement and analytics features. It also handles attendee interaction, reporting and integration with marketing automation.
page.quick_answer: Start by defining the audience outcome and format, then match the cost model and ownership model to your team capacity; a short checklist and a cost‑model table make the decision clear.

sections.h2: What audience outcome and format drive the platform choice?

blocks.p: The desired outcome — lead generation, education, community building or revenue — and the format — single‑track webinar, multi‑track summit or hybrid conference — determine which platform features you need. A lead‑gen webinar needs simple registration, polling and CRM hand‑off, while a multi‑track summit requires agenda management, virtual expo booths and concurrent streaming. Hybrid events add on‑site AV integration and a backup stream.

sections.h2: Which cost model fits your budget and buying process?

blocks.p: Platform pricing falls into three models — per‑host licences tied to attendee capacity, self‑serve monthly subscriptions, and annual contracts negotiated by sales. Per‑host licences (Zoom Webinars) scale with seat count, self‑serve plans (StreamYard, Livestorm) charge a flat monthly fee, and enterprise suites (ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast) require a custom quote.

sections.h2: Who owns the run of show and production on the day?

blocks.p: Clear ownership of the run of show, speaker rehearsals and backup stream prevents last‑minute gaps. Assign a single producer for a simple webinar; for summits and hybrid events add a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator.

ul: Producer – owns run of show and timing
Show caller – cues speakers and transitions
Speaker manager – coordinates rehearsals and tech checks
Platform operator – monitors stream health and backup

sections.h2: What production support do you need beyond the platform?

blocks.p: The platform is software; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations; it does not sell platform licences.

sections.h2: How long does it take to launch a webinar versus a summit?

blocks.p: A webinar typically needs three to four weeks of preparation, while a summit or online conference requires six to eight weeks. Lead time includes brief, production, review, approval, publishing and reporting; a repeat format can move faster.

faq.q: Can I use the same platform for both webinars and hybrid conferences?
faq.a: Many platforms support both single‑track webinars and multi‑track hybrid events, but feature depth differs; verify concurrent streaming, on‑site AV integration and expo capabilities before committing.

faq.q: What is the typical cost range for a produced webinar?
faq.a: Produced webinars generally cost $2,500 to $7,500 per production, covering producer, rehearsal, branded assets, live moderation, backup stream and edited clips.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book a hybrid venue and platform?
faq.a: Lock the venue AV and the platform six to eight weeks before the event date; this allows agenda finalisation, speaker rehearsals and a full technical rehearsal two to five days prior.

faq.q: Does the production partner sell platform licences?
faq.a: The production partner does not sell event software; it produces events on the platform you choose and can help you evaluate options. The team scopes production and operations work per engagement and provides a quote after reviewing your requirements.
